minutes.headline: Board OK'd a July 27 field hockey boot drive and added Ashby to the hazardous waste pact; solar deals tabled.
minutes.summary: The Select Board approved a field hockey boot drive in the town center, a disclosure letting town counsel work on a net metering credit agreement with Townsend, and adding Ashby to the household hazardous waste agreement. It heard from the Green Communities Task Force, tabled the solar power purchase and PILOT items, and discussed an Emerald Place crosswalk. The town manager reported on year-end closeout and state aid, and the board went into executive session on the police union contract.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town pays an annual assessment for access to the Devens facility, about what two collection days cost. Ashby will pay annual and capital assessments, lowering others' annual share.
Year-end wiggle room allowed money to be set aside for codifying bylaws; one bid was received.
Lighting upgrade with Unitil paying half, funded from leftover DPW and facilities money, with a short payback.
Net new revenue after higher choice and charter assessments; Chapter 70 rose and must be appropriated at special town meeting.
A new road treatment was tried on four roads from leftover money; Malpas would cost more.
Accounts payable and payroll warrants were read for the board.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved adding Ashby to the household hazardous waste agreement, with Ashby to pay annual and capital assessments.
The board tabled the solar power purchase agreement and PILOT items until next week.
The board approved a disclosure and consent letting town counsel work on the Townsend net metering credit agreement.
The board approved a July 27 field hockey boot drive in the town center, requested by team captains' parents.
The town manager reported on year-end closeout and the state budget, including Chapter 70 aid that needs appropriation at a special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Adding Ashby to the hazardous waste agreement spreads the facility's annual costs over more towns, which lowers the share other member towns pay.
The state aid that rose this year cannot be spent until a special town meeting appropriates it, so residents may be asked to vote on it.
The tabled solar purchase and PILOT items affect what the town pays for electricity and what a solar developer pays in lieu of taxes.
watch_next: The tabled solar power purchase agreement and PILOT items, due back at the board's next weekly meeting.
A special town meeting article to appropriate the Chapter 70 increase.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the three main votes (boot drive, Ashby HHW amendment, dual-representation consent) and on most of the headline figures. They differ on how the tabled items, resignations and policy meetings are described, on the warrant and road-repair figures, and on attendees: the official minutes name Alonzo and the Town Manager, which ours omit. A reader should check the warrant list and the $18,000 road figure first.
